findings.summary: paapiReplacer missing return in else branch causes TypeError crash when paapiDef is truthy but not an array or function
findings.failure_scenario: A bid interception rule with paapi: 'invalid' (truthy string) passes through the array/func checks, logs an error, but returns undefined. When intercept() later calls match.rule.paapi(match.bid, bidRequest), it throws 'TypeError: match.rule.paapi is not a function'.

findings.summary: intercept() calls addPaapiConfig unconditionally via forEach but JSDoc marks it optional -- throws TypeError if not provided and mockPaapi is non-empty
findings.failure_scenario: Call intercept({bids: [...], bidRequest: {...}, addBid: fn, done: fn}) without addPaapiConfig when a matching rule has a non-empty PAAPI config array. mockPaapi.forEach(cfg => addPaapiConfig(...)) throws 'TypeError: addPaapiConfig is not a function'.

findings.summary: normalizer inner function accesses cd[field] without null guard -- TypeError when consent data is null or undefined
findings.failure_scenario: When no GPP section data exists for a state, getConsentData()?.parsedSections?.[api] evaluates to undefined, flatSection(undefined) returns undefined, and the normalizer's inner function executes cd[field] on undefined consent data, throwing 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined' at the Array.isArray(cd[field]) check.

findings.summary: JSDoc return type changed from {knssoId} to {string|undefined} but getId returns an object {id: string}, not a string
findings.failure_scenario: Developers reading the JSDoc expect getId() to return a plain string or undefined; it actually returns {id: string} on success. Callers checking typeof result === 'string' would incorrectly treat a valid result as invalid.

findings.summary: JSDoc @param {BidderRequest} bidderRequest added to getOpenRTBExtObject which takes zero parameters
findings.failure_scenario: Developers reading the JSDoc believe they must pass a bidderRequest argument; the function signature accepts none, so any passed argument is silently ignored. This is a documentation regression introduced by the PR.

findings.summary: JSDoc says @param {Object} bid but the actual onTimeout function parameter is named timeoutData, not bid
findings.failure_scenario: Developers reading the JSDoc reference the parameter as 'bid' in their mental model; the actual parameter name available at runtime is timeoutData. The previous JSDoc had the correct parameter name timeoutData; this is a regression introduced by the PR.
